title: PredictionAccuracy
description: One prediction resolved against the arrival it predicted. Written by consumers/prediction/job.py, sunk into raw.prediction_accuracy by connect/prediction_accuracy.json. One row is one point on the error curve; consumers/prediction/accuracy.py states the sign convention.

lead_time_s.description: predicted_arrival minus issued_at, both from the PREDICTION. Negative for the ~2.8% of records restating an arrival in the past.

error_s.description: POSITIVE means the prediction was later than reality, so a rider who trusted the sign missed the bus. A sign flip here inverts every conclusion, which is why accuracy_record documents it twice.

lead_bucket.description: One of LEAD_BUCKET_LABELS. Not an enum on purpose: adding a bucket would then be a schema change for no gain, and the bucket set is pinned by dbt tests instead.

route_short_name.description: From the OBSERVATION, because the prediction stream carries no route_short_name. NULL on the late-prediction path, where only the arrival timestamp was kept.

start_date.description: ISO here, unlike the enriched topic's GTFS form. The two topics disagree on purpose; see consumers/prediction/accuracy.py's service_day().

issued_at.description: Epoch SECONDS, as an INTEGER: the TimestampConverter rejects FLOAT64.

predicted_arrival.description: Epoch SECONDS, as an INTEGER, same reason as issued_at.

observed_at.description: Epoch SECONDS, as an INTEGER. The connector partitions on this one, so unix.precision=seconds is load-bearing too.
